posts.title: Two kinds of rain opened Arabia
posts.text: A 500,000-year dust record from the western equatorial Indian Ocean links hominin expansions in Arabia to Green Arabia humid phases, and also to brief, intense rainfall phases within some glacials.
posts.alt: Schematic diagram on an off-white (#FBFBFA) background with a forest-green accent band: two boxes, 'prolonged humid (Green Arabia)' and 'brief, intense rain within some glacials', both point with arrows to a box labelled 'hominin population expansions in Arabia'.

posts.title: When two monsoons fell in step
posts.text: A 450,000-year speleothem record from the Amazon: the South American and Asian monsoons were mostly out of phase, but crossed a synchronicity threshold in ten events, including glacial terminations.
posts.alt: Schematic chart on an off-white (#FBFBFA) background with a forest-green accent band: two wavy lines from 450 ka to today, the South American and Asian monsoon, mostly mirror images; two shaded windows mark where they move in step, with a note on ten synchronous events.

posts.title: Rain and evaporation, told apart
posts.text: Lake Junin, Peru: H and C isotopes of terrestrial and aquatic n-alkanes separate precipitation from evaporation since the LGM. Reduced P-E and local water stress stand out in the mid-Holocene.
posts.alt: Schematic diagram on an off-white (#FBFBFA) background with a forest-green accent band: a box for terrestrial wax (precipitation) and a box for aquatic lipids (evaporation) feed arrows into a box labelled water balance P minus E; a note says reduced P minus E was most evident in the middle Holocene.
